## Load Data

```{r}
# Code to load grade distribution data files:

# Data originally from reddit user austingwalters in this reddit thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/udub/comments/4e6kxl/i_made_a_website_that_shows_grade_distributions/
# Dataset and 2016 FOIA request info from their dropbox: https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/8lbyazjlt5jmv86jvvs06/AGtgMaWeyZtZuS2fSYLYn_4?dl=0&e=1&rlkey=1sg7t372nhslxogwjl3e9lt9t

astbio_grades_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/ASTBIO_grades_2016.csv")
biol_grades_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/BIOL_grades_2016.csv")
cse_grades_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/CSE_grades_2016.csv")
dance_grades_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/DANCE_grades_2016.csv")
design_grades_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/DESIGN_grades_2016.csv")
info_grades_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/INFO_grades_2016.csv")

library("dplyr")
```

## Info Grades

```{r}
glimpse(info_grades_df)
info_grades_num = round(nrow(info_grades_df), 2) # a
info_grades_num
info_grades_mean_num = round(mean(info_grades_df$Student_Count), 2) # b
info_grades_mean_num
info_grades_sum = sum(info_grades_df$Student_Count) # c
info_grades_sum
info_grades_min = round(min(info_grades_df$Average_GPA), 2) # d
info_grades_min
info_grades_max = round(max(info_grades_df$Average_GPA), 2) # e
info_grades_max
info_grades_mean_gpa = round(mean(info_grades_df$Average_GPA), 2) # f
info_grades_mean_gpa
```

Summary: There are `r info_grades_num` total class records to work with in the Info Program. The average student count was `r info_grades_mean_num` students. There were a total of `r info_grades_sum` students in the Info Program. The lowest GPA recorded for the Info program was a `r info_grades_min`, while the highest recorded one was a `r info_grades_max`. The average GPA students had in the Info program was a `r info_grades_mean_gpa`.

## CSE Grades

```{r}
#glimpse(cse_grades_df)
#nrow(cse_grades_df) # a

cse_grades_num

cse_grades_mean_num
cse_grades_sum = sum(cse_grades_df$Student_Count) # c
cse_grades_sum
cse_grades_min = round(min(cse_grades_df$Average_GPA), 2) # d
cse_grades_min
cse_grades_max = round(max(cse_grades_df$Average_GPA), 2) # e
```

Summary: There are `r cse_grades_num` total class records to work with in the CSE Program. The average student count was `r cse_grades_mean_num` students. There were a total of `r cse_grades_sum` students in the CSE Program. The lowest GPA recorded for the CSE program was a `r cse_grades_min`, while the highest recorded one was a `r cse_grades_max`. The average GPA students had in the CSE program was a `r cse_grades_mean_gpa`.

## Analysis

the CSE program seems to be a lot more popular than the Info program, as `r cse_grades_sum` people did CSE, compared to `r info_grades_sum` people in the Info program. The CSE program is generally more difficult to get a higher grade in, as people on average got a `r cse_grades_mean_gpa` in the class, which Info program people on average had a GPA of `r info_grades_mean_gpa`. The lowest GPA for the CSE dataset was a `r cse_grades_min`, while it was a `r info_grades_min` at Info. This shows that people might do worse in CSE than in Info.
